framework: AWS Security Best Practices + PCI DSS v4.0 Mapping
description: Checklist for identifying and assessing AWS resources exposed to the internet, with mappings to relevant PCI DSS controls.

items.title: S3 buckets públicos con datos sensibles
items.description: S3 buckets containing sensitive data (backups, PII, credentials) are configured to allow public read/write access. This is a direct and severe data exposure risk.
items.remediation: Enable 'Block Public Access' at the account and bucket level. Remove any public ACLs or bucket policies. Ensure buckets with sensitive data are encrypted and access is restricted via IAM policies and roles.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires that system components storing cardholder data are not directly accessible from untrusted networks. A public S3 bucket is, by definition, directly accessible from the internet (an untrusted network).

This control mandates that the Primary Account Number (PAN) is rendered unreadable anywhere it is stored. A public bucket makes data readable to everyone, directly violating the core principle of protecting stored cardholder data.
This control requires access to be based on the principle of least privilege. Making a bucket public is the antithesis of least privilege, granting maximum possible privilege to the entire internet.

items.title: S3 bucket policy permite acceso cross-account sin condiciones de seguridad
items.description: S3 bucket policies that grant access to principals in other AWS accounts without strong conditions (aws:SourceAccount, aws:SourceArn, or principal scoping to roles) increase exposure risk. This is not public access, but it expands the trust boundary and can lead to data/log tampering or misuse.
items.remediation: Review cross-account bucket policy statements. Restrict principals to specific IAM roles (not account root) and add conditions such as aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn (for AWS services), or external ID patterns where applicable. Validate with AWS Policy Simulator.

pci_dss.reason: Access must be restricted by least privilege. Cross-account access without strong scoping/conditions expands privilege beyond the required boundary.

items.title: RDS/Databases directamente accesibles desde internet
items.description: Relational Database Service (RDS) instances or other databases are configured with the 'PubliclyAccessible' flag set to true and have security groups allowing access from 0.0.0.0/0.
items.remediation: Set 'PubliclyAccessible' to false for all RDS instances. Place databases in private subnets and restrict access via security groups to only the specific application servers that need to connect to them.

pci_dss.reason: A publicly accessible database is a system component storing cardholder data that is directly accessible from an untrusted network (the internet), which is explicitly forbidden by this control.
Industry-accepted hardening standards universally recommend against exposing databases directly to the internet. This configuration violates secure configuration principles.
Exposing a database to the world violates the principle of least privilege. Access should be restricted to only specific, authorized application components.

items.title: Security Groups con SSH/RDP abierto a 0.0.0.0/0
items.description: Security group rules allow unrestricted access from any IP address (0.0.0.0/0) to administrative ports such as SSH (22) or RDP (3389). This exposes instances to brute-force attacks.
items.remediation: Modify the security group to only allow SSH/RDP access from a trusted, limited set of IP addresses (e.g., corporate office, bastion host). The best practice is to use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager and remove direct SSH/RDP access entirely.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires inbound traffic to be restricted to only what is necessary, with all other traffic denied. Allowing SSH/RDP from the entire internet is not necessary and violates this 'deny-all' principle.

This control requires that non-console administrative access (like SSH/RDP) is secured. Exposing these ports to the world is a failure to properly secure the administrative interface, making it vulnerable to attack.

This finding relates to securing the entry point for non-console administrative access, for which MFA is required. A wide-open port is a failure to adequately protect the administrative interface where MFA would be challenged.

items.title: EC2 con puertos de gestión expuestos (22, 3389, 3306, 5432)
items.description: EC2 instances have public IP addresses and are associated with security groups that expose administrative or database ports directly to the internet.
items.remediation: Place instances in private subnets. Use an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for web traffic. Restrict security group rules to only necessary sources. Use AWS Systems Manager for management.

pci_dss.reason: This requires restricting inbound traffic to only what is necessary. Exposing management and database ports to the internet is a direct violation, as that traffic is not necessary from all sources.
This control requires disabling unnecessary functionality. While the service (e.g., SSH, MySQL) may be necessary for the server, exposing it via an open port is an unnecessary and insecure function.

items.title: Lambda URLs sin autenticación con lógica sensible
items.description: AWS Lambda functions with sensitive business logic are exposed to the internet via a Function URL with the authentication type set to 'NONE'.
items.remediation: Change the Lambda Function URL authentication type to 'AWS_IAM'. Use API Gateway with an authorizer (IAM, Cognito, or Lambda authorizer) as a more robust and secure frontend.

pci_dss.reason: This relates to preventing attacks on business logic and access control. A public Lambda URL with no authentication is a complete bypass of access control mechanisms for that piece of business logic.
Allowing unauthenticated access to sensitive logic is a gross violation of the principle of least privilege.
This control requires that all access to system components and cardholder data is assigned to an individual and authenticated. A Lambda URL with no authentication fails to meet this requirement.

items.title: API Gateway sin autenticación/rate limiting
items.description: API Gateway endpoints that trigger sensitive backend operations are configured without any authentication mechanism (e.g., IAM, Cognito, API Key) and without rate limiting (throttling).
items.remediation: Implement an authorizer (IAM, Cognito, or Lambda) for all sensitive endpoints. Configure Usage Plans and API Keys to enforce throttling and prevent abuse.

pci_dss.reason: An API without authentication allows access without identification or authentication, directly violating this fundamental control.
Public access without authentication is the maximum possible privilege, directly opposing the requirement for least privilege.

While API Gateway itself isn't a WAF, the lack of authentication and rate limiting makes it vulnerable to web-based attacks like business logic abuse and denial of service, which this control aims to prevent.

items.title: ALB/NLB sin WAF en aplicaciones críticas
items.description: An internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) or Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of a critical, public-facing web application does not have AWS WAF associated with it.
items.remediation: Create an AWS WAF Web ACL with AWS Managed Rules (e.g., Core rule set, SQLi rule set) and associate it with the critical ALB.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires an automated technical solution (like a WAF) to be installed in front of public-facing web applications to detect and prevent web-based attacks. This finding is a direct violation.

items.title: Secrets/credenciales hardcodeadas en Lambda
items.description: Sensitive information like database passwords, API keys, or other secrets are stored in plaintext within Lambda environment variables or source code.
items.remediation: Remove secrets from environment variables and code. Store them securely in AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (SecureString type) and grant the Lambda function's execution role permission to retrieve them at runtime.

pci_dss.reason: This control demands processes to protect cryptographic keys and secrets against disclosure. Storing secrets in plaintext environment variables is a direct failure to protect them.
Hardcoding credentials is a common software vulnerability. Secure development practices require separating code from secrets.
This control requires that passwords/passphrases are not stored in a readable format. Hardcoded credentials in environment variables or code are considered readable.

items.title: CloudFront sin protección DDoS (Shield)
items.description: A CloudFront distribution for a business-critical application is not protected by AWS Shield Advanced, relying only on the default Shield Standard.
items.remediation: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced and add the CloudFront distribution to its list of protected resources. This provides enhanced DDoS protection and access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT).

pci_dss.reason: This control is part of incident response and requires measures to prevent, detect, and address DoS attacks. Not having adequate DDoS protection for a critical application is a failure in prevention.

items.title: ALB con TLS 1.0/1.1 (obsoleto)
items.description: An internet-facing ALB is configured with a security policy that allows obsolete and insecure TLS versions 1.0 or 1.1.
items.remediation: Update the ALB listener's security policy to a modern one that enforces TLS 1.2 or higher, such as 'ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06'.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires strong cryptography and security protocols. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are explicitly defined as not being strong cryptography and must not be used for transmitting cardholder data.
This control requires implementing strong cryptography according to industry best practices. Using deprecated TLS versions is a direct violation of this.

items.title: S3 buckets con listado de objetos público
items.description: S3 bucket permissions allow anyone on the internet to list the contents of the bucket, which can lead to inadvertent disclosure of sensitive file names and structures even if the objects themselves are not public.
items.remediation: Modify the bucket policy and/or ACLs to deny the 's3:ListBucket' action for public principals. Ensure that only authorized IAM users or roles can list the bucket contents.

pci_dss.reason: Allowing public listing of objects violates the principle of least privilege. The ability to see what files exist in a storage location is a privilege that should be restricted to authorized personnel.

Allowing object listing is a form of information leakage that is not strictly necessary for the functioning of most applications and should be denied as part of restricting traffic/access to only what is essential.

items.title: S3 bucket policies deben forzar TLS (aws:SecureTransport)
items.description: S3 bucket policies for critical buckets (logs, backups, audit trails) should explicitly deny requests where aws:SecureTransport is false. Missing TLS enforcement can allow accidental misconfigurations or non-TLS access paths for sensitive data/logs.
items.remediation: Add a Deny statement in the bucket policy for s3:* on both bucket and object ARNs with Condition Bool aws:SecureTransport=false. Validate policy behavior with AWS Policy Simulator.

pci_dss.reason: Strong cryptography must be used for transmission of sensitive data. Enforcing aws:SecureTransport helps ensure TLS is used for S3 access.

items.title: S3 versioning debe estar habilitado en buckets de auditoria/logs
items.description: For buckets storing audit trails, configuration history, or log backups (e.g., CloudTrail/Config/log archives), versioning should be enabled to protect against accidental or malicious overwrites and deletions.
items.remediation: Enable S3 versioning on audit/log buckets. Consider S3 Object Lock (WORM) and MFA Delete for high-assurance log integrity.

pci_dss.reason: Audit logs must be protected from unauthorized modification. Versioning helps preserve historical copies and supports integrity controls.

items.title: EC2 sin Instance Metadata Service v2 (IMDSv2)
items.description: EC2 instances are configured to allow IMDSv1, which is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks that can lead to credential exposure. IMDSv2 introduces session-oriented requests that mitigate this risk.
items.remediation: Enforce the use of IMDSv2 on all EC2 instances by modifying their metadata options. Set 'HttpTokens' to 'required'.

pci_dss.reason: This requires hardening standards to address all known security vulnerabilities. The vulnerability of IMDSv1 to SSRF is a well-known issue, and failing to enforce IMDSv2 is a gap in system hardening.

This control requires mitigating common software attacks. While the vulnerability is in the infrastructure, it is often exploited via application-level SSRF flaws. Enforcing IMDSv2 is a defense-in-depth control that mitigates the impact of such application vulnerabilities.

items.title: Lambda function URLs sin autenticacion
items.description: Lambda Function URLs with AuthType=NONE expose unauthenticated invocation paths from the public internet.
items.remediation: Set Function URL AuthType to AWS_IAM or move endpoint behind API Gateway with strong authz/authn controls.

pci_dss.reason: Unauthenticated function invocation enables access-control bypass paths in public-facing application logic.

items.title: API Gateway stages publicos sin proteccion WAF
items.description: Public API Gateway stages lacking WAF controls increase exposure to common web attacks and abuse.
items.remediation: Associate API frontends with AWS WAF and enable request validation, throttling, and authz where applicable.

pci_dss.reason: Public-facing APIs should have automated controls to detect and prevent web-layer attacks.

items.title: ECS/EKS ingress expone servicios criticos a internet
items.description: Containerized workloads exposed through internet-facing ingress without strict boundary controls increase compromise blast radius.
items.remediation: Restrict ingress paths, enforce private networking where possible, and apply least-privilege security group/network policy controls.

pci_dss.reason: Ingress should be restricted to strictly necessary traffic paths from untrusted networks.

items.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch con acceso publico o politicas debiles
items.description: Search domains with public endpoints or permissive access policies may allow unauthorized data access and enumeration.
items.remediation: Use VPC-only domain endpoints, tighten access policies to specific principals, and enable authN/authZ controls.

pci_dss.reason: Data-store access must be constrained to authorized principals under least privilege.

items.title: CloudFront con origen S3 sin control de acceso de origen fuerte
items.description: CloudFront distributions using S3 origins without clear origin access restriction (OAI/OAC) can expose direct-bucket access and increase unauthenticated enumeration paths.
items.remediation: Enforce private S3 origins behind CloudFront using Origin Access Control (recommended) or Origin Access Identity, and block direct public S3 access.

pci_dss.reason: Publicly reachable object-store paths should be minimized and restricted to necessary edge delivery controls.
Origin access should be restricted to explicit service principals and least-privilege paths.

items.title: API Gateway expone metodos de mutacion sin autenticacion fuerte
items.description: Public API routes supporting POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE without strong authorization increase risk of unauthenticated business-logic abuse and direct data manipulation.
items.remediation: Require IAM/Cognito/JWT/Lambda authorizers for mutating routes, enforce explicit deny-by-default policies, and validate access control tests for every stage.

pci_dss.reason: Mutating operations must require authenticated and uniquely attributable identities.
Unauthenticated mutation paths are a common API security weakness enabling abuse and unauthorized actions.

items.title: API Gateway con rutas catch-all (ANY/proxy) sin auth
items.description: Wildcard API routes such as ANY /{proxy+} without authorization broaden attack surface and can bypass intended route-level restrictions.
items.remediation: Avoid unauthenticated wildcard routes, scope explicit methods/paths, and require strong authorizers for generic proxy handlers.

pci_dss.reason: Broad wildcard routing without authentication violates least privilege and increases unauthorized-access paths.

notes: Generated based on aws-exposure-checklist.md and mapped against PCI DSS v4.0 controls.
